factoryData.readme:
# Subagent Architecture (V1)

Dev-time **subagents** for the factory — specialized Codex agents that Codex spawns in parallel
and collects into one result (codebase exploration, review, verification). Reference:
Codex *Subagents* docs.

> **Not the same as `agents/`.** `agents/` holds the factory's **product agents** (Python packages
> on `agent-core` that ship in the pipeline). Subagents here are **dev-workflow orchestration** —
> they operate *on this repo* during development. Different layer, different purpose.

## Folder layout

```
.codex/
├── config.toml            # [agents] global orchestration settings (max_threads, max_depth)
└── agents/
    ├── README.md          # this doc
    └── _template.toml     # reference subagent — copy it to add one
```

One `.toml` file = one subagent. Codex identifies it by its `name` field (match the filename by
convention). Project-scoped agents live here; personal ones go under `~/.codex/agents/`.

## Config schema

Every subagent file **must** define:

| Field | Required | Purpose |
|---|:---:|---|
| `name` | ✔ | how Codex spawns/refers to the agent |
| `description` | ✔ | when Codex should use it |
| `developer_instructions` | ✔ | the agent's core behavior |

Optional (inherit from the parent session when omitted): `model`, `model_reasoning_effort`,
`sandbox_mode` (`read-only` / `workspace-write`), `mcp_servers`, `nickname_candidates`,
`skills.config`.

## Global settings (`.codex/config.toml`)

```toml
[agents]
max_threads = 6   # concurrent open agent threads (default 6)
max_depth   = 1   # nesting depth; 1 = a child can spawn but not grandchildren (default 1)
```
Keep `max_depth = 1` unless you truly need recursive delegation — raising it turns broad
delegation into repeated fan-out (more tokens, latency, resource use).

## Suggested subagents (add as needed)

None are shipped yet — create them from `_template.toml` when a workflow calls for it. Keep each
narrow and opinionated, one job, `read-only` unless it must run something. Good first candidates for
this repo:

- an **explorer** — maps the monorepo (`libraries/`, `agents/`, `libraries/models/blocks/`), cites
  files, proposes no fixes.
- a **reviewer** — correctness, security, and **missing offline tests** (the factory's bar).
- a **verifier** — runs the offline suites (`scripts/test-all.sh` or a package's `pytest`).

## Add a subagent

```
cp _template.toml <name>.toml    # then set name/description/developer_instructions
```
Codex spawns subagents only when explicitly asked, e.g.:
> "Have `explorer` map the affected blocks, `reviewer` find real risks, and `verifier` run the
> offline suites — then summarize each."
